summary: Require distinct declared execution units and deterministic bounded-handoff chaining for credited Adaptive Execution passes, then revalidate the merged Adaptive Execution behavior under the corrected discipline.
reason: Revision-8 Adversarial passed under convergence mode, then revision-8 Interdependency identified a material producer-consumer deadlock between the staged revalidation sequence and the generated-queue contract. Both SKILL.md and shared-control-model.md required update_revalidation_queue.py --check to pass before stage advancement while the checker intentionally remains nonzero for unresolved later stages/evaluations. Under those rules together, Adversarial could never validly hand off to Interdependency. The authorities now distinguish ordered inter-stage advancement from final completion: the regenerated queue must be current, the completed/current and all earlier required stages must have valid evidence, and no earlier prerequisite may be unresolved; unresolved later stages/evaluations remain scheduled and block final completion rather than progression to the next required stage. A fully current and clear --check remains mandatory before final completion/merge. Because this correction changes canonical behavioral authority after revision-8 Adversarial credit, review_revision is incremented to 9 and revalidation reopens at Adversarial. The revision-8 Interdependency pass receives no credit. Historical execution occurrences remain preserved in the append-only ledger.

adversarial_convergence.trigger: The separated-pass architecture already exceeded the three-retry convergence threshold during revision 8; revision 9 continues the same bounded architecture after an Interdependency authority-contract correction.
adversarial_convergence.blocking_rule: Only findings that threaten a declared core invariant, permit false credit or protected-control bypass, materially overstate assurance, invalidate required mapped/downstream conclusions, or expose a genuinely new reusable attack class may invalidate the next Adversarial pass.
adversarial_convergence.nonblocking_rule: Minor documentation, redundant hardening, low-impact edge cases, optional diagnostics, and other observations that do not threaten the core invariants are recorded or deferred and do not cause a restart.
core_invariants: No false semantic stage or execution-pass credit can be accepted by the governed completion path.
Required separated/subdivided execution order and bounded handoff chaining cannot be bypassed by backfilling multiple passes into one durable execution state.
A durably completed pass or stage plan cannot be replaced, mutated, replayed, or redone without the required review-revision reopening semantics and new execution identities.
Current and partial execution evidence cannot be accepted under a stale review revision, stale gate, or stale governed artifact state.
Historical/base-state evidence and the closed exemption boundary prevent reuse or omission that would falsely legitimize current execution evidence.
Repository checks and records do not claim to prove an actual host message/context or isolation boundary when the host supplies no independently trustworthy boundary identity.
adversarial_convergence.next_pass_requirement: Classify every new material Adversarial observation as blocking or non-blocking against these invariants before making any correction.
